name: Old Towns of Djenné
description: Djenné rises from the floodplain of the Niger and Bani rivers in central Mali, a town of earthen houses that has been lived in since about 250 B.C. It grew rich as a market and a stop on the trans-Saharan gold trade, and later became a centre of Islamic learning. Nearly 2,000 traditional houses still stand, many raised on mounds called toguere to stay above the seasonal floods. The site is currently on the List of World Heritage in Danger.
